subject: APAC region pinning confirmation + subprocessor mapping request
messages:
From: Sofia Patel <sofia@zephyrhealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@zephyrhealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: APAC region pinning, backups, and subprocessor mapping

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the call earlier. Before we move forward on the PO, a couple of items legal/procurement asked me to confirm in writing:

1) APAC pinning: Can Redwood commit to keeping all customer content and request-level logs originating from our tenant strictly within APAC (Singapore and Tokyo regions) for both active inference and long-term backups? We need contractual language that prevents cross-border replication of raw customer content.

2) Cross-region processing: We understand that for DR/failover there may be exceptions, but Procurement insists on a clear threshold and notice requirement. Please confirm the exact circumstances in which Redwood would process data outside of APAC and whether pseudonymization/obfuscation is applied prior to any cross-region processing.

3) Subprocessors / SCIM: We need a mapping of any identity/SCIM providers and any other subprocessors that handle config or user provisioning for our tenant. Ideally a CSV with columns: name, role, region, contact, and whether they have access to customer content.

4) SOC2 + DPA evidence: Please attach the latest SOC2 and your DPA; we will loop legal if there are changes.

Can you get back to me with a written confirmation and the requested artifacts? Procurement hopes to sign next week if we can get the APAC pinning addendum in place.

Thanks —
Sofia Patel
Head of Product, Zephyr Health
sofia@zephyrhealth.ai

[Attachment requested: SOC2_report_redacted.pdf (we will accept redacted copy)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia@zephyrhealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: APAC region pinning, backups, and subprocessor mapping

Hi Sofia —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then details and next steps.

- APAC pinning: Yes — we support pinning customer content to APAC for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we can configure regional routing so inference and storage are kept in APAC regions (Singapore, Tokyo) and we can offer an addendum that prohibits cross-border replication of raw customer content for backups and long-term storage.

- Cross-region processing: For Hosted we do have limited, documented failover policies. If a regional outage requires DR, we will only fail over to a pre-approved region and will apply in-flight protections: TLS across hops, at-rest encryption with customer or Redwood-managed KMS (customer choice), and ephemeral pseudonymization for logs where feasible. We can include explicit thresholds in the addendum (e.g., outage duration > 30 minutes and regional capacity < 5% for > 2 consecutive minutes).

- Subprocessors/SCIM: Attached is our current subprocessor dump (redwood_subprocessors_q4_2025.csv) and a draft APAC pin addendum (APAC_pin_addendum_draft.docx). The CSV highlights SCIM/identity providers and which subprocessors have access to any customer content.

- SOC2 + DPA: DPA v3 is attached and we can provide an SOC2 Type II redacted report via secure link — happy to share that with Procurement.

Neha and Karthik — can you confirm whether the Hosted failover thresholds above are accurate and whether we can commit, contractually, to the "no cross-border replication of raw content" language (subject to documented DR exceptions)? Also, can Infra confirm whether backups are replicated cross-region for Hosted by default and whether we can switch replication off per-tenant?

Sofia — if this looks good I can circulate the addendum and request procurement sign the DocuSign link. If Procurement needs different SLA thresholds or explicit notification windows, tell me what you need and we will try to accommodate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, redwood_subprocessors_q4_2025.csv, APAC_pin_addendum_draft.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sofia Patel <sofia@zephyrhealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 14:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: APAC region pinning, backups, and subprocessor mapping

Thanks for looping us in. A few compliance/legal clarifications:

1) Contractual commitment: We can sign an addendum that restricts storage and processing of "raw customer content" to APAC regions for Hosted when configured and for all Dedicated/Private deployments. We should define "raw customer content" explicitly (requests and model outputs, stored artifacts, log payloads containing PII) and exclude aggregated telemetry/operational metrics which are pseudonymized.

2) DR/failover exception: We cannot promise absolute zero cross-border processing in all scenarios. Proposed binding language: "Redwood will not process or replicate raw customer content outside the APAC region except when necessary for continuity of service in the event of a documented regional outage or catastrophic infrastructure failure. Such processing will be limited in scope, applied for the minimum time necessary, and Redwood will notify Customer within 24 hours of the event. Redwood will apply pseudonymization to request logs prior to any cross-region replication where full content is not strictly required to restore service."

3) Backups: Karthik — per-tenant cross-region replication can be toggled for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we currently replicate snapshots to a secondary region for backups; we can offer a customer-level opt-out but it will affect RTO/RPO guarantees and may carry a surcharge. We should capture the surcharge in procurement discussions.

4) Subprocessors: The CSV is good; recommend we flag the SCIM provider(s) and any identity vendors in the DPA addendum as "supporting subprocessors" with limited scope (provisioning only). Also recommend adding a contractual right for quarterly subprocessor notices and a 30-day review window for critical subprocessors.

I'll draft language for the addendum (short, bulletized) and share a version today. From a legal perspective the proposed failover threshold Marissa suggested (outage > 30 minutes AND capacity < 5%) is reasonable but let's frame it as "operationally defined outage" and avoid hard numbers where possible; Procurement may push back and ask for numeric thresholds — we can surface that in negotiation.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com

[Attachment: proposed_APAC_pin_clause.txt — short clause for addendum]

From: Sofia Patel <sofia@zephyrhealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@zephyrhealth.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: APAC region pinning, backups, and subprocessor mapping

Marissa/Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the helpful language. A couple of follow-ups from Procurement:

- Procurement will accept the operationally defined outage wording but is asking for a notification SLA of 24 hours (written) and a post-incident report for any event where cross-region processing was used. Is that acceptable?

- On backups: Zephyr can accept a Hosted opt-out of cross-region snapshot replication if Redwood confirms the surcharge and impact to RTO/RPO in writing in the addendum. Please include the surcharge line item and updated RTO/RPO table.

- Subprocessors: please confirm that SCIM providers listed in the CSV do NOT have access to stored customer model outputs or raw request payloads — only provisioning metadata. If so, we can close that item.

If you can incorporate these small updates into the DocuSign draft we can route internally and aim to sign by EOD next Tuesday.

Thanks —
Sofia
